summary: the abort classifier casts a chain adapter's rejection to `Error`: a thrown string prints `undefined` into the failure signature, a thrown `null` raises past `Dispatcher.tick`
acceptance: `grep -n 'as Error' src/tickAttempt.ts` empty — the classifier reads its two abort keys off a guarded shape and its message through the one fold, so a chain adapter's non-`Error` rejection records the thrown text as a preempt instead of raising inside the catch. One home left in `src/` for that fold: `src/thrown.ts` carries `throwFacts` too, moved out of `src/tickVerdict.ts` with that header's claim shrunk to a pointer, and `thrownMessage` computes from it rather than respelling `String(err)`. The ~30 inline `instanceof Error ?` reads across `src/` and `harness/` stay — debt, out of scope. `Error`-path text byte-identical, so no standing expected string moves. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` green.
tests: an agent adapter rejecting with a string classifies as the pre-exit error class naming the thrown text
an agent adapter rejecting with null classifies as a platform preempt instead of raising inside the classifier
notes: Measured this tick via two probes through `preemptFrom` (`tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:13067`), then reverted. A string rejection yields `agent process error before exit: undefined` — also the signature the consecutive-identical backstop compares on, so distinct rejections collapse to one. A `null` rejection raises `TypeError` at `src/tickAttempt.ts:608`, escaping `runAttempt` (:327), `src/singletonTick.ts:275` and `src/Dispatcher.ts:1055`. The thrower is chain code (`Phase.agent:756`).
